headline: Biodiversity is life's variety—and variety provides resilience, options, and discovery potential
universal_truth: Variety is strength; monocultures are fragile; diversity provides insurance against the unknown
fun_facts: Scientists have identified about 2 million species, but estimates suggest 8-10 million exist
Losing species loses potential—many medicines come from obscure plants and animals
The Irish Potato Famine happened because a single variety dominated—when disease hit, everything failed
discussion_questions: Where do you rely on variety for resilience?
What are the risks of too much sameness?
How do you cultivate diversity in your life or work?

hook.script: A forest with 100 tree species can lose one and survive. A monoculture plantation can be wiped out by a single disease. Variety is strength. Biodiversity isn't just beautiful—it's insurance against disaster.

cliff.script: We often optimize for uniformity—standardization, efficiency, predictability. But nature shows variety's value. What does biodiversity teach us?

options.text: Diversity provides options for unknown futures—different species handle different conditions, so variety ensures some will thrive no matter what happens
options.response: Yes. You can't predict which species will matter. But with variety, something will be suited to whatever comes. Diversity is a hedge against uncertainty.

options.text: Diversity is just aesthetic—variety is nice to look at
options.response: It's beautiful, yes, but the functional value is even greater—resilience against change...

fact1.title: Resilience Through Variety
fact1.script: Diverse ecosystems recover from disturbance faster. If one species fails, others fill the gap. Monocultures have no backup. Variety is built-in insurance.

fact2.title: Unknown Value
fact2.script: We don't know which species might cure cancer or provide food security. Losing species loses potential we haven't discovered. Extinction is irreversible loss of options.

fact3.title: Personal Diversity
fact3.script: Your life benefits from diversity too: diverse skills, relationships, experiences. Overdependence on one thing creates fragility. Cultivate variety in what matters.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Variety is strength. Monocultures are fragile. Diversity provides insurance against the unknown. Cultivate it.

outro.script: That's Day 259. Tomorrow, we'll explore outsiders taking over—invasive species. Until then, consider where you need more diversity.

growTrack.title: Diversity Audit - Where's Your Variety?
growTrack.activity: Where in your life do you have healthy variety—skills, income sources, relationships, interests? Where are you over-concentrated in a 'monoculture'? Consider adding diversity where you're too dependent on one thing.
